competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight tape pairs firm equities with a modest volatility lift: the S&P holds near 7541 while the VIX has moved up to 21.15. Energy eased versus the prior session, with Brent at 103.60 after fading from about 104.77 and WTI at 96.09—still consistent with Hormuz shipping diplomacy and Iran tanker-mine headlines, not stale oil-bearish stories against these marks. Gold stays elevated near 3940. ECB FX shows a firmer dollar/yen at 158.29, AUD/NZD still crowded near 1.2417 at the top of its one-year range, and soft NZD/USD at 0.5624 near the bottom. Front-end disconnects remain wide: cash-versus-March leftovers sit near 41–44bp on SOFR, CORRA, and TONA, with Canada March implieds cheapening to 2.97 while the SOFR strip still prices a Fed hold. Sovereign 10-year yields stay rich, including US 4.95%. causal.original_belief: The NZ-US 10-year residual at -23bp was NZ rich to the United States, a transitory cross-market dislocation that would mean-revert toward a zero differential rather than mark a new fair-value NZ premium.
causal.observed_reality: Over about 20 days the residual closed to zero and the short was flattened at that anchor; the sleeve was then frozen to research-only, so the same rates-RV ticket cannot be reopened even if the spread later overshoots.
causal.assumptions_right: The -23bp print was a residual, not a regime; mean-reversion to the zero anchor was the realization, and flattening there matched the stated reaction function instead of hunting a new NZ policy shock.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Underweighted that permission would flip to research-only at the same moment the residual completed, removing any option to fade an overshoot in NZ sovereign space, and underweighted that a zero print can be both thesis-complete and the floor of the old residual.
causal.causal_divergence: The result came from residual closure, not from a dated RBNZ or U.S. coupon catalyst. The research-only constraint is a mandate change, not evidence that NZ-US 10s are fairly valued from here.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Knowing the residual would retrace to zero and that new NZ sovereign tickets would be research-only, the close at the zero anchor is still the correct trade; holding past zero for a NZ-cheapening overshoot would have been a new, unpermitted ticket.
causal.future_implication: Do not reopen NZ_10Y or NZ-US_10Y. If kiwi cheapness reappears, express it in markable FX such as AUDNZD or NZDUSD, not in frozen NZ rates-RV.

postmortems.what_worked: The minus-23 basis-point residual mean-reverted to the stated zero anchor, and flattening there matched the reaction function instead of hunting a new New Zealand policy shock.
postmortems.what_failed: The research-only mandate flip arriving at the same moment the residual completed was underweighted, so there was no option to fade a later overshoot in New Zealand sovereign space.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The original thesis that the residual was transitory and would close toward zero was realized; the result came from residual closure, not a dated catalyst.
postmortems.expression_assessment: The rates-RV sleeve was the correct expression until it became research-only; remaining kiwi cheapness belongs in markable FX.
postmortems.lesson: When an RV residual completes at its stated anchor in a sleeve that is becoming research-only, flatten and migrate any remaining country view into a still-tradable FX expression rather than inventing a new rates ticket in the frozen sleeve.
